correctness.rationale: For an irreducible curve other than L and exceptional E_i, Bezout with the common line gives Σm_i≤d and hence C²=d²−Σm_i²≥0; its class lies in the cone of L,E_i, making nefness equivalent to nonnegative intersections with these generators. The only negative supports are exceptional subsets and mixed L+I of |I|≤n−2, whose matrix Schur complement is −(n−1−|I|). Orthogonality gives λ=(Σ_{j∉I}b_j−a)/(n−1−|I|) and μ_i=λ−b_i, bounding all reduced denominators by divisors of 1,…,n−1. The explicit integral effective D_r=rH−Σ_{j∈J}E_j has N_r=(L+Σ_{i∈I}E_i)/r and nef P_r, with exact denominator r; adding nef big Q_r preserves N_r. All allowed supports are realized by big divisors, giving chamber count 2^(n+1)−n−1. Pure-Python rational checker verifies representative n≤24 and all steps are proved for n≥3.

value.rationale: The distinction between largest reduced coefficient denominator and the least universal simultaneous clearing multiple is mathematically motivated in the primary work: effective application of Zariski decompositions requires a common multiplier. The exact least lcm is a natural unknown invariant, with explicit witnesses for every intermediate denominator and exact chamber support structure. It is not a numerical recomputation of the earlier maximum denominator; the new assertion explains the full divisibility spectrum rather than just its endpoint.
